region.name: Western Jezero Delta + Adjacent Crater Floor

scope.main: Volume 2 Delta Front, 5 site groups and 9 sample records
scope.optional: Volumes 1, 3, 4 within numeric bounds, 10 additional site groups and 14 records

limitations: Inventory-derived project dataset; not a NASA-issued JSON dataset.
Coordinate linkage, vertical-datum compatibility and registration acceptance remain pending.
Valid point support does not establish regional gap-free coverage, absolute accuracy or route safety.
Reported elevations have unresolved datum; do not use as renderer heights or merge CTX and HiRISE heights.
Runtime coordinate conversion, marker anchoring and UI tests remain integration work.
Group names combine naming levels; slash labels are not independently verified synonyms.

sites.label: Roubion
sites.scienceSummary: Atmospheric sample; no rock core recovered. The target is a mafic rock with evidence of alteration by water. This is useful as sampling-history context, not a recovered rock core.
sites.markerPolicy: Use representative sample coordinates only as a provisional group anchor; preserve individual sample coordinates; never spread overlapping samples geographically.

sites.label: Rochette
sites.scienceSummary: Fine-grained mafic rock, probably igneous; the report retains basaltic sandstone as an alternative. Plagioclase and pyroxene occur with secondary sulfates and other alteration minerals.
sites.markerPolicy: Use representative sample coordinates only as a provisional group anchor; preserve individual sample coordinates; never spread overlapping samples geographically.

sites.label: Brac
sites.scienceSummary: Olivine-rich cumulate rock with pyroxene. Sulfates, carbonates and hydrated phases record aqueous alteration; reported organic material does not establish life.
sites.markerPolicy: Use representative sample coordinates only as a provisional group anchor; preserve individual sample coordinates; never spread overlapping samples geographically.

sites.label: Issole
sites.scienceSummary: Olivine-pyroxene cumulate rock with relatively limited aqueous alteration. Carbonate and hydrated sulfate provide a comparison with other crater-floor targets.
sites.markerPolicy: Use representative sample coordinates only as a provisional group anchor; preserve individual sample coordinates; never spread overlapping samples geographically.

sites.label: Sid
sites.scienceSummary: Interpreted in the initial report as likely basaltic andesite, with feldspar and pyroxene. Secondary minerals and hydration indicate limited alteration; interpretation is preliminary.
sites.markerPolicy: Use representative sample coordinates only as a provisional group anchor; preserve individual sample coordinates; never spread overlapping samples geographically.

sites.label: Skinner Ridge
sites.scienceSummary: Sandstone interpreted as deposited in a prodelta environment. Diverse transported grains and probable iron-magnesium carbonate cement support study of sediment transport and alteration.
sites.markerPolicy: Use representative sample coordinates only as a provisional group anchor; preserve individual sample coordinates; never spread overlapping samples geographically.

sites.label: Wildcat Ridge
sites.scienceSummary: Fine sedimentary mudstone interpreted as lake-deposited, with magnesium-iron sulfates and calcium-sulfate veins. Fluorescence may reflect aromatic organics; that inference is not evidence of life.
sites.markerPolicy: Use representative sample coordinates only as a provisional group anchor; preserve individual sample coordinates; never spread overlapping samples geographically.

sites.label: Amalik
sites.scienceSummary: Olivine-bearing mudstone interpreted as lake-deposited. Altered olivine and relatively little sulfate distinguish it from Wildcat Ridge; possible organic-related signals remain tentative.
sites.markerPolicy: Use representative sample coordinates only as a provisional group anchor; preserve individual sample coordinates; never spread overlapping samples geographically.

sites.label: Hidden Harbor
sites.scienceSummary: Fine sandstone interpreted as lake-deposited, rich in magnesium-iron sulfate with calcium-sulfate patches. Mineral and fluorescence measurements provide another comparison of sediment alteration.
sites.markerPolicy: Use representative sample coordinates only as a provisional group anchor; preserve individual sample coordinates; never spread overlapping samples geographically.

sites.label: Observation Mountain
sites.scienceSummary: Loose regolith containing coarse grains, sand and silt, with likely dust. Mixed primary and secondary minerals allow comparison of unconsolidated material with bedrock cores.
sites.markerPolicy: Use representative sample coordinates only as a provisional group anchor; preserve individual sample coordinates; never spread overlapping samples geographically.

sites.label: Berea / Tenby
sites.scienceSummary: Sandstone interpreted as river-deposited, with basaltic grains and carbonate/sulfate alteration. Useful for comparing Upper Fan sediments with Delta Front materials.
sites.markerPolicy: Use representative sample coordinates only as a provisional group anchor; preserve individual sample coordinates; never spread overlapping samples geographically.

sites.label: Emerald Lake
sites.scienceSummary: Mixed-clast conglomeratic sediment interpreted as river-deposited. Diverse grains, altered olivine and carbonate-bearing material record transported source-rock diversity.
sites.markerPolicy: Use representative sample coordinates only as a provisional group anchor; preserve individual sample coordinates; never spread overlapping samples geographically.

sites.label: Dream Lake / Hague Creek
sites.scienceSummary: Poorly sorted sandstone interpreted as river-deposited. Olivine, pyroxene and feldspar occur with carbonate matrix and silica-rich cross-cutting material.
sites.markerPolicy: Use representative sample coordinates only as a provisional group anchor; preserve individual sample coordinates; never spread overlapping samples geographically.

sites.label: Hans Amundsen Memorial Workspace / Mandu Wall
sites.scienceSummary: Possibly sandstone with altered basaltic composition, carbonates and silica. Depositional environment and even sedimentary versus altered igneous origin remain uncertain in the initial report.
sites.markerPolicy: Use representative sample coordinates only as a provisional group anchor; preserve individual sample coordinates; never spread overlapping samples geographically.

sites.label: Turquoise Bay / Lake Newell
sites.scienceSummary: Possibly sandstone with altered basaltic composition, magnesium-iron carbonates and sulfates. Formation setting is unresolved; silica may act as cement.
sites.markerPolicy: Use representative sample coordinates only as a provisional group anchor; preserve individual sample coordinates; never spread overlapping samples geographically.
